title: Euler-product form of the trace formula
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type
$k_0$-scheme, and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let
$\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$ and let $K$ be a Weil complex with
coefficients in $\Lambda$ satisfying the hypotheses of
[thm-trf-trace-formula-e] (if $\Lambda=E$) or of
[thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar] (if $\Lambda=\Qlb$). These are
only the finite-level hypotheses (explicit etale-origin witnesses and
compactification admissibility for the reductions of a lattice of an
$E$-representative $K_E$). The Weil map $\varphi_E$ of $K_E$ is an
isomorphism of $D^b_c(X,E)$, but it need not be integral, or invertible
on any lattice after any rescaling. Write
$F=F^{\,1}_{c,K}$ for the global geometric Frobenius on
$H_c^i(X,K)$, and for a closed point $x\in|X_0|$ of degree
$e_x=[\kappa(x):\Fq]$ write $F_x$ for the one-circuit local Frobenius
on the stalk $K_{\bar x}$ (well defined up to conjugation). Put

$$
\det\bigl(1-T^{e_x}F_x\mid K_{\bar x}\bigr)
:=\prod_{j\in\mathbf Z}
\det\bigl(1-T^{e_x}F_x\mid H^j(K_{\bar x})\bigr)^{(-1)^j},
\qquad
L(X_0,K,T)=\prod_{x\in|X_0|}
\det\bigl(1-T^{e_x}F_x\mid K_{\bar x}\bigr)^{-1}.
$$

Then:

1. The product defining $L(X_0,K,T)$ is locally finite for the
$T$-adic topology, and $L(X_0,K,T)\in1+T\Lambda[[T]]$.
1. As formal power series in $\Lambda[[T]]$,
$$
L(X_0,K,T)=\prod_{i\in\mathbf Z}
\det\bigl(1-TF\mid H_c^i(X,K)\bigr)^{(-1)^{i+1}},
$$
the product being finite.
1. If $\dim X_0\leq1$ and $K$ is a sheaf placed in degree zero, then
$H_c^i(X,K)=0$ for $i\notin\{0,1,2\}$, so the product in (2) runs
over $0\leq i\leq2$:
$$
L(X_0,K,T)=
\frac{\det(1-TF\mid H_c^1(X,K))}
{\det(1-TF\mid H_c^0(X,K))\,\det(1-TF\mid H_c^2(X,K))}.
$$
1. For every field embedding $\iota:\Qlb\to\mathbf C$, applying
$\iota$ coefficientwise carries the identity (2) (for $\Lambda=\Qlb$)
to the corresponding identity in $\mathbf C[[T]]$.

proof.text: For a finite-dimensional vector space over the characteristic-zero field $E$, [lem-weil-exp-trace-determinant] gives $\det(1-TG)^{-1}=\exp(\sum_{r\ge1}\operatorname{Tr}(G^r)T^r/r)$ for every endomorphism $G$. Over $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, [lem-zl-euler-product-identity] gives the same formula for the cohomological Frobenius modules constructed in Step 2. This is the logarithmic-determinant route of blueprint Step 0; no integral Weil structure is required. For a finite graded family, put $S_i=\sum_{r\ge1}\operatorname{Tr}(G_i^r)T^r/r$. The finite-sum identity of [lem-weil-power-series-exp-hom] gives $\exp(\sum_i(-1)^iS_i)=\prod_i\exp(S_i)^{(-1)^i}=\prod_i\det(1-TG_i)^{(-1)^{i+1}}$; the negative signs use $\exp(S_i)\exp(-S_i)=\exp(0)=1$. Substituting $T^e$ for $T$ gives the local identity with $T^{er}$. For an infinite family whose terms have orders tending to infinity, the same identity holds coefficientwise: by [def-weil-power-series-exponential], the coefficient of $T^N$ in $\exp(U)$ depends only on $U$ modulo $T^{N+1}$, so the finite-sum identity passes to the $T$-adic limit.

Work over $E$, using the operators and normalized stalk transports explicitly supplied by [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model]. Write $g=g_\gamma$, $B_m=g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$ and $\varphi=\varphi_E$. The definition of the iterates as a product of $m$ pullbacks of $\varphi$ gives $\varphi^{[m+n]}=\varphi^{[m]}\circ Lg^{m*}\varphi^{[n]}$ by splitting that product after its first $m$ factors. Naturality and composition of the supplied integral base-change identifications remain equalities after [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]. Thus, with the object subscripts understood, $B_1R\Gamma_c(\varphi^{[m]})=R\Gamma_c(Lg^*\varphi^{[m]})B_1$ and $B_1B_m=B_{m+1}$, whence
$$F_{c,K_E}^1F_{c,K_E}^{\,m}=R\Gamma_c(\varphi\circ Lg^*\varphi^{[m]})B_{m+1}=F_{c,K_E}^{\,m+1}.$$
The base case is $m=1$, so $F_{c,K_E}^{\,m}=(F_{c,K_E}^1)^m$ for all $m\ge1$.
For the local calculation use only the geometric orbit assertion (1) of [lem-trf-local-frobenius-conjugacy], which does not involve coefficients. Above a closed point $x$ of degree $e$, label the geometric lifts $z_i=g^iz_0$, with indices modulo $e$. Put $V_i=K_{E,z_i}$. Via the canonical pullback-stalk identifications and normalized fixed-point identifications of [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model], the stalk of $\varphi$ is an isomorphism $A_i:V_{i+1}\to V_i$. The identifications are natural and compatible with composition, so the stalk of $\varphi^{[m]}$ with its fixed-point transport, for $m=er$, is the product $A_iA_{i+1}\cdots A_{i+m-1}=C_i^r$, where $C_i=A_i\cdots A_{i+e-1}$. If $T_i=A_0\cdots A_{i-1}:V_i\to V_0$, with $T_0=1$, then the two products $C_0T_i$ and $T_iC_i$ consist of the identical ordered list of $e+i$ factors. Hence $C_i=T_i^{-1}C_0T_i$ and $F_{z_i,m}=T_i^{-1}C_0^rT_i$. This proves both lift independence of the conjugacy class of $F_x=C_0$ and the power formula over $E$, without applying a finite-coefficient lemma to $E$. The scalar-extension statement of [thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar] proves the corresponding assertions over $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Finally [thm-trf-trace-formula-e] and that scalar extension give bounded finite-dimensional compact cohomology and stalk cohomology. Thus each inverse local determinant lies in $1+T^{e_x}\Lambda[[T]]$, and the global determinant product is finite.

For each $r\ge1$, [thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points] makes $X_0(\mathbf F_{q^r})$ finite. The geometric orbit assertion (1) of [lem-trf-local-frobenius-conjugacy] gives exactly $e_x$ lifts of a degree-$e_x$ closed point in $X_0(\mathbf F_{q^{e_x}})$. Consequently the closed points of degree at most $N$ are images of the finite union of these rational-point sets for $1\le r\le N$. Each $e_x$ is positive, so no factor contributes below degree $e_x$ and only finitely many contribute through degree $N$. The Euler product therefore converges coefficientwise, and $T$-adically, in $1+T\Lambda[[T]]$. This proves clause (1) and justifies every rearrangement below. For $N=0$ all factors are $1$ modulo $T$.

Fix $m\ge1$. By the orbit assertion (1) of [lem-trf-local-frobenius-conjugacy], a closed point $x$ has rational lifts in $X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ exactly when $e_x\mid m$, with $e_x$ lifts in that case: on its cyclic orbit of length $e_x$, $g^m$ fixes every point precisely when $e_x\mid m$. The calculation in Step 2 of this split gives $F_{y,m}$ conjugate to $F_x^{m/e_x}$ on each lift. Conjugacy induces conjugacy on every cohomology space, hence equality of their ordinary traces (also [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws], clauses (1) and (4)). Therefore [thm-trf-trace-formula-e], or [thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar], gives
$$\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(F^m\mid H_c^i(X,K))=\sum_{e_x\mid m}e_x\,t_x(m/e_x),\qquad t_x(r)=\sum_j(-1)^j\operatorname{Tr}(F_x^r\mid H^j(K_{\bar x})).$$

Multiply the trace identity of Step 4 by $T^m/m$ and sum over $m\ge1$. Reindexing $m=e_xr$ gives
$$\sum_{m\ge1}\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(F^m\mid H_c^i(X,K))T^m/m=\sum_x\sum_{r\ge1}t_x(r)T^{e_xr}/r,$$
since $e_x/m=1/r$. Step 3 makes this reindexing finite in every coefficient. Apply the formal exponential to both sides. The finite alternating determinant identity established in Step 1 identifies the left-hand side after exponentiating with the finite alternating cohomological determinant product. On the right, [lem-weil-power-series-exp-hom] and the coefficient formula of [def-weil-power-series-exponential] (Step 1) allow exponentiation through the locally finite sum; the determinant identity with $T^{e_x}$ in place of $T$ identifies the $x$-factor with $\det(1-T^{e_x}F_x\mid K_{\bar x})^{-1}$. This proves clause (2) directly, without requiring an uncited logarithm theorem.

Assume $\dim X_0\le1$ and $K$ is a sheaf in degree zero. First work over $E$. Choose an integral representative $K_{\mathcal O}$ using [thm-trf-trace-formula-e]. The equivalence and closure clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] apply: $X$ is noetherian, finite dimensional, and $\ell$ is invertible. They give bounded integral cohomology sheaves with finite stratified finitely presented module models, and closure under standard truncations. The integral t-structure is [prop-weil-pbc-integral-tstructure]; the rational truncations are [prop-constructible-truncations]. Localization is t-exact because it sends integral nonpositive and nonnegative objects into the corresponding classes defined in [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure], and sends their truncation triangles to truncation triangles. Hence $\mathcal H^j(K_{\mathcal O})$ rationalizes to zero for $j\ne0$. By the raw Hom-localization definition [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], its identity is killed by a power of $\varpi$. A bounded complex whose cohomology objects are killed by powers of $\varpi$ is itself killed by a power: in a triangle, if powers $\varpi^a,\varpi^b$ kill the two outer objects, exactness of Hom factors $\varpi^a$ on the middle object through the other outer object, so $\varpi^{a+b}$ kills it; induct on truncation triangles. Thus the two truncation cones outside degree zero vanish in the rational category.
Let $C=\mathcal H^0(K_{\mathcal O})$, and let $D=C[\varpi^\infty]$. Its finitely presented local models on a finite stratification have bounded torsion exponent; taking a finite refinement on the quasi-compact strata gives a single exponent for $D$. On these models $M=C/D$ is finitely generated and torsion-free, hence finite free over the DVR by [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free]. The characterization theorem therefore puts $D$ and $M$ in the integral category. Since $D$ is killed by a power, $K\cong M[1/\varpi]$. The reductions $M_n=M\otimes^L A_n=M/\varpi^nM$ are constructible sheaves, flat over $A_n$ on every stratum, hence of Tor amplitude $[0,0]$, and tensor associativity gives $M_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n\cong M_n$. No Weil structure on $M$ is asserted or required.
By clauses (1),(2) of [prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems], $P=R\Gamma_c(X,M)$ has a bounded finite-free $\mathcal O_E$ model with $P\otimes^LA_1\cong R\Gamma_c(X,M_1)$. By [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], $H_c^i(X,K)=H^i(P)\otimes E$. Choose a compactification of $X_0/k_0$ by [thm-nagata-compactification], replace its ambient scheme by the scheme-theoretic closure of $X_0$, and base change to $k$. The resulting $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ is a compactification with $\dim\bar X\le1$: both dense-open invariance and field-extension invariance are [lem-kun-dimension-extension]. By [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison], the constructible finite-coefficient sheaf $M_1$ has an explicit etale-origin representative. Apply [lem-trf-compactification-cohomology] to identify $R\Gamma_c(X,M_1)$ with $R\Gamma(\bar X,j_!M_1)$. The sheaf $j_!M_1$ is constructible (use the strata for $M_1$ and the complementary stratum with value zero), so [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] and [sk-prop-sf-comparison] identify its cohomology with etale cohomology of a torsion sheaf. The field $k$ has torsion cohomological dimension zero by [lem-sf-separably-closed-torsion-cd]; [thm-sc-finite-type-torsion-cd] then makes this cohomology vanish for $i>2$, and a sheaf has no negative cohomology. Finally, the short exact sequence of complexes $0\to P\xrightarrow{\varpi}P\to P/\varpi\to0$ gives an injection $H^i(P)/\varpi H^i(P)\hookrightarrow H^i(P/\varpi)$. For $i\notin\{0,1,2\}$ its target is zero. The finitely generated module $H^i(P)$ is therefore zero by [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson], applied to the maximal ideal $(\varpi)$ of $\mathcal O_E$. In particular $H_c^i(X,K)=0$ in those degrees. For $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, [prop-constructible-truncations] commutes with common-stage scalar extension, and faithfulness of extension of fields makes the representing $E$-object a sheaf; the cohomology scalar extension in [thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar] gives the same vanishing. Substituting the three surviving degrees in clause (2) gives the displayed fraction, proving clause (3).

A field embedding iota:Q̄_l→C is a ring homomorphism. Its coefficientwise extension to formal power series preserves addition and multiplication coefficient by coefficient, inverses of series with constant term 1, and determinants because determinants are finite sums of products. Each coefficient of the locally finite Euler product is computed from finitely many factors, so applying iota to clause (2) gives the corresponding identity in C[[T]].

Finite alternating products follow from the exponential homomorphism.
Generic formal exponential homomorphism used in blueprint Steps 0 and 4; the infinite-sum extension is proved coefficientwise in this split.
Integral local-model and truncation properties needed to justify the sheaf lattice constructed in blueprint Step 5; no statement within the unit supplies them.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q69-5870d7a62 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the full delivery: item, all 7 steps, every cited statement, and the blueprint main-20261015 statement and proof (Steps 0-6). The master and main statement bodies are identical, and the node statement matches them exactly, so nothing is weakened. Small cases checked: Spec F_q with a scalar Weil map; Spec F_{q^2}, where the degree-2 point gives 1-T^2 and F swaps the two summands; A^1, where H^2_c=E(-1) and L=1/(1-qT); the empty scheme. Step 0: clauses (1),(2) of prop-trace-determinant hold over any characteristic-zero field, the sign of Delta matches, and the substitution T->T^e and the coefficientwise infinite sum follow from def-weil-power-series-exponential. Step 1: recomputed the global composition F^1F^m=F^{m+1} through the rational transport. Recomputed the cyclic products: C_0T_i=T_iC_i=A_0...A_{i+e-1}, so C_i=T_i^{-1}C_0T_i, with T_i invertible because phi_E is an isomorphism. Only the geometric clause (1) of the conjugacy lemma is used. Steps 2-4: X_0(F_{q^r}) is finite by thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points; the grouping by closed points and the trace invariance under conjugacy follow from trace formal laws (1),(4); the reindexing m=e_x r is finite in each coefficient. Step 5 (curves): checked t-exactness of localization through the standard pair; the raw Hom localization; the torsion bound of the local models; M_n flat; adic-systems clauses (1),(2) need no Weil structure; the closure of the Nagata compactification has dim<=1 by lem-kun-dimension-extension; the etale-origin witness, the compactification comparison and cd<=2d+c<=2; H^i(P)/varpi injects into H^i(P/varpi), then Nakayama. In the Q-bar-ell case E may need to be enlarged first; this is harmless because only a lattice is needed. Step 6 is elementary. The DAG is acyclic, proof_deps equals the union of the uses lists, and there are no new nodes or duplicates.
